annotationRationale: Slope determines each horizontal run from the common vertical rise, locating the axis intercepts. Their distance is then the difference of their horizontal coordinates.
sourceMethod: Follows the second official method using rise and run, with the intercept coordinates made explicit.

review.mathCheck: A rise of 30 requires positive horizontal runs 30/2=15 and 30/6=5. Consequently the intercepts are (25,0) and (35,0), whose distance is 10, choice B. The positive slopes justify placing both intercepts left of the intersection.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution #3's second approach on page 2. The candidate adds explicit intercept coordinates to the official rise-and-run calculation.
review.annotationCheck: Using the slope formula inversely to recover horizontal run is appropriate. Intercept finding is assessed, and distance along the x-axis is supporting knowledge. No graph or additional method is needed.
